component.name: Maprisma
component.summary: Your AI agents, models and tools on one map

description.p: Maprisma shows the AI setup on your computer as cards and a map: coding agents with their plan, limits and usage, local LLMs and their models, MCP servers and skills. Connect them by drawing a line, with a preview and Undo.

ul.li: See what each agent still needs, with the command that fixes it
Install local LLMs and download models; they start and stop with their agents
Find MCP servers and skills on your computer or on the web
A health check: what works, what to fix, and what the setup is good for

description.p: On Omarchy, the same app is the AI Agents Map plugin.

Hardening from a security review: programs run for a short job end together with everything they started; local requests and downloads have one deadline each; a program folder other accounts could change is refused and the checked download is the one unpacked; terminal paste is size-limited; model files must be regular files; folder scans stay within a budget; skills from the web come from one commit, every file checked.

F12 saves a picture of the window privately in your Pictures folder, with an optional note about what is wrong. Settings › Corners has a new choice, Slightly rounded (6 px), and every control follows the setting. Smart cards take your own suggestions per category.
Add-ons left over from Asterism, this app's old name, no longer show as "Not available in this version": their card says what they are and that removing them lets Maprisma use its own copy.

Strata joins the local LLMs: Maprisma finds it, shows its models, starts and stops it, connects agents to it and can install it. Settings › Map › Show faded lines can hide the lines of other boxes while one is selected. Odd replies from a local LLM server and odd port numbers no longer disturb the map.

The map shows what this PC already has: at the first start everything found is switched on, agents installed outside a package count, and programs and local LLMs to install sit at the end of their cards. Agents show their real sign-in (keyring, moved home), plan limits and costs as batteries, and an online agent signs in only to its own provider. A provider's chosen model follows its agents, two MCP servers of one name stay apart, Settings has sections with Find, and Ask AI uses the same menus as the map, with its own Undo. Repair edits only provider entries it can read safely.

Fixes the map that turned grey whenever one agent used another. The map now reads skills or MCP → agent → provider → model, one line per step and only real connections; the "only what is connected or pinned" filter hides models nobody uses. Drawing a local provider onto one of its models is one short step, and an agent connected to that provider later gets the model. Tasks handed to an agent ("Do it with …") stay in a private file instead of the command line.

A calmer map: lines show only real connections, red only marks a real problem, and agents working together get their own colour with an arrow to the agent they use. Drawing a line asks in a small dialog and confirms with a note and Undo; a drop that cannot work says why. Ask AI can make every change you can draw on the map, through the same preview, and suggests example questions for each part of the map.

Asterism is now Maprisma: a Flutter app with its service in Dart, nothing of Python in it. Your Asterism settings come along at the first start. On Omarchy it opens as a popup under the bar (maprisma --toggle). New: daily AI checks for MCP server updates, a local helper on your own LLM, recent changes with Undo after a restart, keyboard shortcuts and accessibility checks, safe updates of running agents, usage figures from Omarchy, and add-ons signed with a new key.

Everything AI on this PC is on the map: MCP servers and skill folders that no agent uses yet are faded boxes, and a line from an agent connects one (nothing is connected by itself). Setup's Local MCP servers and Skills get Add folder… for places such as a shared disk with apps and skills, and servers at a web address get a card of their own. The first open shows what is found in an animated overview. Also: cards on the map fold and a pin keeps the layout; Terminals… and Stop… for agents started outside the window; Ask an agent which model or MCP server fits; agents installed with mise start from the app launcher; safer model moves and many hardening fixes.

Subagents get a page of their own: a mark on the agent's box opens their map with each one's task, working ones lit and finished ones dimmed (Settings › Subagents). An arrow joins two agents when one started the other. What every agent's tokens cost at API prices: a cost label for agents paid per token, coloured against a day's limit, and an API cost card on its page with input, output and cache per model, in dollars or euros (Settings › Costs). Token counts are read for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, Oh My Pi, OpenClaw, Crush, DeepSeek Harness and Goose, a new agent. Also: Smart Check, the usage box on a working agent's line, a lighter map animation and less work in the background.

The user manual catches up with 0.10.0, in all eight languages: models at once and the GPU memory check before an agent starts, the violet lines, the network page, Configure…, reordering the header's symbols, the Information page and a new picture of the main window.

A new local LLM or a new agent is now one add-on: the app asks each local LLM's engine and each agent's facts and never names them, and templates plus a guide show how to make one. Local LLMs that serve several models get a models-at-once setting with GPU memory warnings, also before an agent starts; different models of one local LLM get violet lines.

Each agent has a network page (traffic in and out, where it goes), the header's symbols can be reordered by dragging, and an Information page lists the author's other plugins. Configure… opens an agent's or local LLM's own setup in a terminal. Connect pages and the MCP page share a clearer layout; Oh My Pi connects to local LLMs; freshly installed local LLMs are found and explained.

Play chess against your agents. Claude Code, Codex, Hermes and Pi can be asked for one move at a time, without tools, in an empty private folder: a chess page with a board that turns to your side, captured pieces beside it, a thinking time that sets how long and how strongly the agent plays, and a game that keeps running in the background with a button in the header and on the agent's box.

Local LLMs that hold GPU memory get a stop button that asks first (free the memory or stop it). LM Studio open without its server says so and offers Start server; the model it has loaded is marked, with a light line to it when no agent uses it. A new agent's web look-up no longer fails.

Safer commands and clearer texts. Commands run in a terminal window quote every word, the API key command's answer and the skill writer's answer file are read with a size limit, and the key file is written as a new private file. Hints no longer point at the map's old "+" boxes but at Setup. The manual says exactly when a password is asked (installing an agent that comes as a system package) and names the right version.

Setup (formerly My setup) and Map are on every page, Setup first. A red ! in the header lists open problems, each with a button to where it is fixed, and updates and suggestions; cards with a problem show the same red !. Online agents show a battery for what is left of their limits, and running local LLMs one for the GPU memory still free. The map runs across the whole width, starts agents with ▶ on their boxes, shows unused connections as red dotted lines and, in a narrow window, picks what to show by itself. A card explains the first connection and Setup explains in five steps how things get onto the map. Agents are now described as data: their add-ons bring facts instead of code, and extension add-ons can add to an agent. With Insights 1.1.0 the Topics card shows which topics took the most tokens. The user manual comes in eight languages and opens in the app's language.

My setup: one page of cards for everything the map shows. Agents, local LLMs and online providers are switched on and off there; MCP servers, skill folders and models each have a card with a menu to update, start, open, uninstall, remove or move, and a card to add more. Cards with an update waiting show the new version. The map now shows only what is set up: no dashed boxes, no Hide and no "+ Available" any more. Lists of MCP servers, models and skills and the map's boxes are cards with icons, and the user manual is new.

A welcome page for a new Asterism: the agents, local LLMs and online providers as cards with their icons, grouped by kind, the ones found on this PC ticked; a click on a card ticks it, one button switches them on. It shows at every start while nothing is switched on. Settings has an About section with the version and a link to the project on GitHub; the health check line stays away while the map is empty. MCP servers show the skills written for them, whether those still match the server's tools, and Update skill rewrites one with a preview and Undo.

Add-ons: every agent and local LLM Asterism understands is now a signed add-on, and a new Set up page switches on the ones installed on this PC with one click. The Add-ons page lists them with search, details and a homepage button, installs more from the signed catalog, takes a dropped .zip or link, and suggests an add-on when a new agent appears. Agents and local LLMs can be installed and removed from their cards, in a terminal inside the window (sudo asks for your password there). Session numbers per project for OpenCode and Hermes too; session titles and the summary by Claude are now the Insights add-on.

Check for updates (Add MCP › On this PC) moves every app that provides an MCP server to its new version in one step, with one preview, backup and Undo, and then tests each updated server. Models moved to the trash in LM Studio leave the map. Help shows LLM Monitor as a small animation in your theme's colours, and the user manual has new screenshots.

A Healthy & Security check on every agent's details page shows what the agent may do without asking you, explains every setting and choice with its risk, changes them with a preview and Undo, and lists what lowers each risk; local LLMs show whether only this PC can reach them. Help shows the disk space of agents, local LLMs and models. Pin boxes on the map, right-click menus with the cards' actions, move models between folders by dragging. The user manual has a new chapter on security.

An ⓘ legend in the header explains every dot, line and mark of the map. Hide puts away the agents and providers you don't use (a provider only while no shown agent uses one of its models); + Available lists them under Hidden with Show again. Terminal tabs above the map and the terminals show which agents are working, running or ended. The scroll bar no longer covers the cards' arrows in a narrow window.

Agents run in the window: Start here or in a terminal window, Stop on the card, and running agents show a green icon in the cards and the new tree sidebar. Agent details show herdr's live state and Claude Code's subagent runs. The map lights up along the lines of agents that are working. The models page follows LM Studio's layout. Back returns to the page you came from, an opened card scrolls fully into view, the install page has bigger buttons, and the health check line shows only when something needs fixing.

Downloads never write through a link someone planted in a shared model folder (the half-finished file is created new or resumed only when it is your own). Settings fit the window: two columns when it is wide, framed choices, shorter explanations.

Claude Code's details: your last 30 days per project (working time, sessions, tokens, lines changed, API value), topics under Claude Code's own session titles, and an optional written summary by Claude from those titles and numbers.
